summary:
Fixed and verified — `test.sh` passes.

The needle was a type-coercion bug in `utils.js:22`: `min_rating` was stored as a string (`"4"`) while `min_price`/`max_price` were properly parsed. Downstream in `filter.js`, `buildRatingRange("4", 5)` pushes the string `"4"` on the first iteration (then `i++` coerces it to a number), producing `["4", 5]`. Because `Array.includes` uses strict equality, `"4" !== 4`, so products rated 4 were silently dropped — e.g. `min_rating=4` returned only the 5-star products.

The fix is a one-liner: parse it with `parseInt(..., 10)` like the other numeric query params. All three test cases now pass.
